html:
The Shang dynasty ruled in the Yellow River valley of northern China from about 1600 to 1046 BCE. It is the earliest Chinese dynasty attested by its own writing, on oracle bones from about 1250 BCE.

Later Chinese histories said the Shang came after the Xia and before the Zhou. For a long time no one could prove it existed. Then, from the 1920s, excavations at Yinxu near Anyang uncovered the last Shang capital: palace foundations, royal tombs, chariot burials and tens of thousands of inscribed bones.

What the Shang left:

  • Oracle bone inscriptions, the oldest Chinese writing. Kings asked their ancestors about harvests, war, hunting, weather and childbirth, and the answers were read in cracks in heated bone.
  • Bronze ritual vessels of great size and skill, used to feed the ancestors.
  • Rich tombs, such as that of Fu Hao, a consort of King Wu Ding and a general, found untouched in 1976.
  • Human sacrifice on a large scale at royal funerals and rites.

The king was at the centre of religion. He alone could ask the royal ancestors and the high god Di for help. The Shang fought their neighbours constantly and used captives as sacrifices.

Shang was not alone in China. Far to the southwest, the people who made the Sanxingdui bronzes had their own very different culture.

Around 1046 BCE King Wu of the Zhou defeated the last Shang king at the Battle of Muye. The Zhou later justified this with the idea that the Shang had lost the Mandate of Heaven. Before the Shang came the Erlitou culture, which may be the Xia.
sum: The Shang dynasty ruled in the Yellow River valley of northern China from about 1600 to 1046 BCE. It is the earliest Chinese dynasty attested by its own writing, on oracle bones from about 1250 BCE.
